history-diffs.summary: Git history is a graph of immutable, content-addressed objects. Knowing how refs, revision syntax and range notation walk that graph lets you answer "what changed, where and when" precisely.
points: Objects: blobs hold content, trees map names to blobs and subtrees, commits point to one tree plus parents; IDs are hashes, so identical content is stored once.
Branches are refs holding one commit ID; HEAD is usually a symbolic ref to a branch and becomes "detached" when it holds a commit ID directly.
`~n` walks first parents; `^n` picks the n-th parent of a merge; `ref@{n}` reads the reflog; `@{u}` is the upstream and `@{-1}` the previous branch.
In log, `A..B` is "in B, not in A" and `A...B` is the symmetric difference. In diff, `A..B` equals `A B` and `A...B` diffs from the merge base to B.
`git diff` is working tree vs index, `--staged` is index vs HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is working tree vs HEAD.
`-S` finds commits that change how often a string occurs; `-G` finds patches with matching lines; `-L` traces a line range or function; `--follow` tracks one file across renames.
`--first-parent` shows the mainline with one merge per feature; `--since` filters on committer date, which rebases reset.
traps: `git diff main..feature` is not what a pull request shows; use `main...feature`.
`HEAD~2` and `HEAD^2` are different commits whenever merges are involved.
Commits made on a detached HEAD are not deleted when you switch away, but they become unreachable and expire with the reflog.
